# Privacy Stage Contracts

One entry per desk in the Privacy Data Protection Command Desk suite. Use these when running the suite as a continuous program of work, so a desk can carry work into the next stage instead of telling the user to invoke another skill.

## Stage order

```text
privacy-applicability-desk
  -> data-inventory-mapping-desk
  -> lawful-basis-desk
  -> transparency-notice-desk
  -> consent-preference-desk
  -> cookie-tracking-governance-desk
  -> data-minimization-desk
  -> privacy-by-design-desk
  -> dpia-desk
  -> childrens-data-desk
  -> cross-border-transfer-desk
  -> processor-vendor-agreement-desk
  -> rights-request-intake-desk
  -> rights-request-fulfillment-desk
  -> retention-deletion-desk
  -> breach-assessment-desk
  -> breach-notification-desk
  -> privacy-program-metrics-desk
```

The order is a dependency chain, not a mandatory itinerary. Most engagements run a subsequence and enter partway: a DSAR enters at `rights-request-intake-desk`, a suspected incident enters at `breach-assessment-desk` on a clock that is already running, a new feature enters at `privacy-by-design-desk`, a vendor renewal enters at `processor-vendor-agreement-desk`, and a consent banner complaint enters at `cookie-tracking-governance-desk` and pushes backward into notices and lawful basis. Never run a stage ahead of the packet state it consumes, and never skip a stage the source facts show is load-bearing for the requested outcome.

Two dependencies are structural rather than conventional. Nothing downstream of `data-inventory-mapping-desk` is reliable beyond that desk's coverage statement, because a system nobody read is not a system with no personal data in it. Nothing in rights handling, retention, transfers, or breach scoping works without the data map at some granularity, because "where does this person's data live" and "who was affected" are both graph traversals rather than recollections.

Each entry states the hard halt specific to that stage. The default posture everywhere else is to proceed with the assumption labeled inline against the activity, request, transfer, or notification it affects, per `references/halt-taxonomy.md`.

## Contracts

### privacy-applicability-desk
Requires: legal entities and their establishments, where individuals are located and how the organization reaches them, what the business does with personal data at activity level, sectoral activities such as health, financial, telecom, employment, education, or advertising, processing scale and headcount, group structure and intra-group arrangements, contracts that impose privacy obligations, and any standing position from counsel.
Owns: regime applicability per entity with the provision that brings it into scope and the trigger that satisfies it, controller, joint controller, processor, service provider, or third party determination per processing relationship tested against who actually decides purposes and means, DPO and representative appointment triggers with the contact route each has to publish, sectoral overlays, the regimes explicitly ruled out with the reason each was ruled out, and the accountability documentation each applicable regime obliges the organization to keep.
Hands to: `data-inventory-mapping-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A determination that a regime does not apply, or that the organization is a processor rather than a controller, is a legal position a regulator will test and a contract will be read against. The role label a signed agreement uses does not override who decides purposes and means, and a wrong role assignment misplaces every obligation downstream of it, so the position belongs to counsel or the accountable executive.

### data-inventory-mapping-desk
Requires: system and service inventory, schemas and catalog exports, discovery or scan output, integration, export, and reporting inventory, business process interviews for what the schema does not show, existing RoPA, vendor list, storage regions, backup and log inventory, and the applicability output that says which regimes the map has to satisfy.
Owns: processing activity records built around purposes rather than around systems, a data element inventory per store with classification and identifiability state, special category and criminal offence flags traced to the element that raises them, the data flow map including tags, SDKs, replication, analytics egress, exports, and remote access paths, residency per store, shadow copies found outside sanctioned systems, an accountable owner per activity, and the coverage statement naming which systems were actually read and which were only listed.
Hands to: `lawful-basis-desk`.
Hard halt: connector unreachable. A data map's only useful property is its coverage, and a system that could not be read is not a system with no personal data in it. Every later stage, from DSAR scoping to breach population counts, inherits this coverage figure, and it is the one number in this domain that cannot be estimated.

### lawful-basis-desk
Requires: processing activity records with their purposes, data categories including special category flags, the nature of the relationship with the individual, contract terms where contractual necessity is claimed, the statutory duty where legal obligation is claimed, published notice text at its current version, consent records where consent is claimed, existing basis determinations, and secondary uses already in flight.
Owns: basis selection per activity with the necessity argument stated as why the purpose cannot be met with less rather than why the processing is useful, special category conditions with the additional requirement each condition carries, completed legitimate interests assessments covering purpose, necessity, balancing against the individual's reasonable expectations, safeguards, and the objection route, compatible use assessments for secondary purposes, the basis-change record where a basis was switched mid-processing, and the activities where no basis holds, stated as unlawful processing rather than as a documentation gap.
Hands to: `transparency-notice-desk`.
Hard halt: source conflict. The notice tells individuals one basis and the register or the observed system behavior shows another. Both readings are preserved, because the notice is the version the individual relied on, and choosing whichever reading keeps the activity lawful launders a guess into a legal position that a complaint will later test.

### transparency-notice-desk
Requires: processing activity records carrying purposes, bases, recipients, transfers, and retention, every surface where collection happens including forms, SDKs, call centers, and offline channels, current notices with versions and effective dates, the sources of indirectly collected data, languages and accessibility requirements, the rights and complaint routes that actually work, and automated decision details where any exist.
Owns: notice architecture across layers and surfaces, disclosure coverage checked element by element against what each applicable regime requires, notice at collection and just-in-time notices placed at the moment they are needed, the source disclosure where data was not collected from the individual, the version and effective date record, the change log with a determination of whether a change is material enough to require telling existing individuals rather than just republishing, and the specific disclosures that are missing named individually rather than a verdict that the notice is adequate.
Hands to: `consent-preference-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A published notice is a public statement the organization is held to by every regulator and every individual who read it, and it becomes the criterion later findings and complaints are written against. Publication belongs to the accountable owner with counsel, and a notice cannot be quietly unpublished once people have relied on it.

### consent-preference-desk
Requires: the activities relying on consent, capture surfaces with the wording as currently shown, the consent record schema and what it actually stores, withdrawal paths, preference center implementation, notice versions in force at capture, marketing and communication channels, opt-out and universal signal handling, and CMP or preference platform configuration.
Owns: consent design per purpose with granularity, the freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous test applied to the wording a person actually saw rather than to the policy, the consent record schema including timestamp, notice version, wording, and the identifier consent attaches to, withdrawal made as easy as the original grant, refresh triggers when purpose or wording changes, opt-out and universal signal handling recorded at the layer where the signal changes behavior rather than where it is received, the invalid-consent population with the defect named per record, and a disposition for processing already carried out under invalid consent.
Hands to: `cookie-tracking-governance-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A lawfulness claim would rest on consent records that cannot reproduce what the person was shown when they agreed. That claim travels into the RoPA, into the notice, and eventually into a regulator response, and once the original wording is unrecoverable the only remedy is re-consent across the whole population.

### cookie-tracking-governance-desk
Requires: tag and cookie scan output taken on the live page set including authenticated, checkout, and form paths, tag manager configuration, CMP configuration and its observed behavior before any interaction, the vendor behind each tag, SDK inventory for mobile surfaces, advertising and measurement contracts, the purposes claimed for each tracker, and prior classifications.
Owns: tracker inventory with vendor, purpose, storage duration, and category, the strictly necessary determination made against the purpose the tracker serves rather than against the vendor's own category, what fires before consent measured on the surface rather than read from configuration, CMP behavior including reject symmetry and the absence of pre-ticked or implied consent, universal opt-out signal enforcement with the point in the stack where it takes effect, session replay, fingerprinting, and pixel-based measurement treated as the processing they are and pushed back into the RoPA, unidentified trackers named as unidentified, and a disposition per tracker with the owner who will action it.
Hands to: `data-minimization-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. Unidentified tags or SDKs are running on surfaces that carry personal data and their recipient cannot be established, so the organization cannot state who receives what. This is halted rather than assumed because the usual shortcut, attributing an unknown tag to the vendor it resembles, produces a confident and wrong recipient list that then goes into the notice and the RoPA and is relied on by everyone downstream.

### data-minimization-desk
Requires: the data element inventory with evidence of actual use, processing activity purposes, query and access logs showing which fields are read and by what, analytics and model training uses, de-identification techniques already in place with their key custody, the auxiliary data available inside and outside the organization, and the statutory or contractual reasons a field is retained.
Owns: field-level necessity determinations tied to a named purpose, collection and propagation reductions placed at the surface where the reduction actually lands, pseudonymization, tokenization, aggregation, and generalization choices with the key or mapping custody that keeps them meaningful, re-identification risk assessments naming the auxiliary data considered and the person who assessed it, the boundary between pseudonymized data that remains in scope and anonymous data that leaves it, and the fields nobody could justify listed with the system that keeps producing them.
Hands to: `privacy-by-design-desk`.
Hard halt: source conflict. A dataset is labeled anonymous somewhere in the record while the assessment shows it re-identifiable in combination with data the organization already holds. Both readings are preserved, because an anonymous label removes that dataset from every other control in this suite at once, including retention, rights handling, and breach notification.

### privacy-by-design-desk
Requires: the feature or change with its data flows, product requirements and design artifacts, default settings as configured rather than as available, existing privacy requirements and paved-road patterns, the release stage and the engineering owner, access, telemetry, and analytics plans, retention intent, and prior design decisions on the same surface.
Owns: privacy requirements written as acceptance criteria an engineer can implement and a reviewer can check, defaults assessed as defaults, deceptive pattern review across consent, sharing, and deletion flows, data flow review for collection the feature does not need, access and telemetry design, the threshold determination that escalates a change into a full assessment, and a gate state of cleared, cleared with conditions, or blocked with each condition named and owned.
Hands to: `dpia-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Clearing a change for release is a gate decision with a named owner. A conditional clearance whose conditions nobody accepted is an uncleared change wearing a clearance label, and the release it unblocks is the point where the exposure becomes real.

### dpia-desk
Requires: the processing activity record with purpose, scale, data categories, and data subject vulnerability, systematic monitoring or automated decision details, the technology involved, the design review output, existing assessments and the program's screening criteria, published regulator screening lists where they exist, the security measures relied on, and consultation input from the privacy office, security, counsel, and where appropriate the individuals affected or their representatives.
Owns: the threshold determination with the criteria that triggered it, a systematic description of the processing, necessity and proportionality measured against the purpose, risks written as harms to individuals such as discrimination, exclusion, financial loss, distress, loss of confidentiality, or loss of control over their own data, each with likelihood and severity on a named scale, mitigations mapped to the specific risk each reduces with the residual risk after it, automated decision analysis covering the logic explanation, the significance of the effect, the human review route, and the opt-out, sign-off with a name and a date, the prior consultation determination where high residual risk survives, the review trigger, and the record of whether processing began before the assessment existed.
Hands to: `childrens-data-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Where high residual risk remains after mitigation, the processing does not proceed on the strength of the assessment: it goes to prior consultation with the supervisory authority and to the accountable owner. The timing is itself the obligation, so a launch that outran its assessment is reported as such rather than smoothed by backdating the sign-off.

### childrens-data-desk
Requires: whether the service is directed to children or likely to be accessed by them, the actual and estimated age distribution, what the organization already knows about ages, age assurance options with the data each collects in order to work, parental consent mechanisms and the evidence they produce, current default settings, profiling and advertising configuration, applicable codes and sectoral rules, and any school, guardian, or institutional relationship the data arrives through.
Owns: the audience determination with what it rests on, the knowledge standard the organization is held to, an age assurance approach weighed against its own privacy cost, verifiable parental consent method and evidence where consent is the route, high-privacy defaults for minors across geolocation, profiling, discoverability, sharing, and engagement nudges, restrictions on targeted advertising and profiling, shortened retention for minors, and the transition rules when a user ages into or out of the regime.
Hands to: `cross-border-transfer-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. Continuing would apply an adult default, an advertising configuration, or a profiling behavior to a population the evidence shows includes children, and that exposure lands on the individuals rather than on the organization. Where the age distribution is merely unknown this desk proceeds on the protective assumption and labels it, which is the opposite of the usual posture and is deliberate.

### cross-border-transfer-desk
Requires: the data flow map with destination countries and importers, processor and sub-processor locations including support, administrative, and remote access paths, group entity arrangements, executed transfer instruments with their dates and modules, adequacy status for each destination, the importer's local legal environment, technical measures with the location of the keys, and any localization or residency requirement with its source.
Owns: a transfer inventory keyed to the flows that create it, including remote access and support paths that are transfers without a file moving, mechanism selection per transfer with the module or annex matching the parties' actual roles, executed-versus-drafted state with the execution date, transfer impact assessments covering the destination legal regime, the specific government access powers considered, available redress, and whether the supplementary measures actually defeat the access route identified rather than merely sounding protective, onward transfer obligations, localization constraints, and uncovered transfers named one by one rather than summarized.
Hands to: `processor-vendor-agreement-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Executing a transfer instrument, or accepting supplementary measures as sufficient against an identified access power, is a legal position that a named signatory takes on behalf of the organization. A transfer already running with no executed mechanism is escalated on the day it is found rather than filed as a gap, because data already sent cannot be recalled.

### processor-vendor-agreement-desk
Requires: the vendor inventory with what each processes and on whose instruction, executed agreements and their data protection terms, sub-processor lists and notification mechanisms, security schedules, vendor attestations and questionnaire responses, the transfer inventory for the same vendors, retention and deletion commitments, incident notification terms, joint controller candidates, and procurement stage and renewal dates.
Owns: role determination per relationship tested against who decides purposes and means rather than against the label the contract uses, agreement coverage clause by clause across instruction-only processing, confidentiality, security measures, sub-processor authorization and notice, assistance with rights requests and with breach notification, audit rights, and deletion or return on termination, the sub-processor register with the objection route and its window, service provider or contractor terms where a regime mandates specific language, joint controller arrangements with the essence made available to individuals, the deletion commitment tested against what the vendor can technically do, and vendors receiving personal data with no executed agreement listed by name.
Hands to: `rights-request-intake-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Sending personal data to a vendor with no executed data protection agreement is the violation rather than a step toward one, and an agreement signed after the data arrived does not reach back over what already went. Onboarding belongs to the data owner with legal review wherever the regime or the data category requires it.

### rights-request-intake-desk
Requires: the request as received with its channel and date, the identity signals that came with it, the account or records it may attach to, authorized agent or guardian documentation where someone acts for another, the regimes this requester can invoke given their location and relationship, the existing request log, the identity verification policy and the assurance levels it sets, and the exemption catalogue with citations.
Owns: classification into the specific right under the specific regime rather than into a generic access request, requester type and authority, identity verification at an assurance level proportionate to the sensitivity of what will be disclosed and recorded with the method used, the statutory deadline computed from the receipt date with the regime that set it, extension eligibility with the ground the regime allows, scope definition covering which records and which period, the exemptions that may apply each with the provision it rests on, fee or refusal determinations with the manifestly unfounded or excessive basis stated, and the acknowledgement sent to the requester.
Hands to: `rights-request-fulfillment-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. Proceeding past unverified identity risks disclosing personal data to someone who is not the individual, which is a breach committed while answering a request made under the same law. A failed verification is not a reason to go quiet either: the refusal, its basis, and the appeal route go back to the requester inside the same deadline.

### rights-request-fulfillment-desk
Requires: the verified request with its scope, deadline, and exemptions, the data map and system inventory that says where to look, the processor list filtered to those holding in-scope data, backup, archive, and export inventory, third-party personal data appearing in the same records, the format and delivery channel the right entitles the requester to, prior responses to the same individual, and the portability format where portability applies.
Owns: retrieval across every system the map identifies, with the systems searched and the systems not searched both named, processor instructions issued and their responses tracked, redaction of third-party personal data and exempt content with the basis recorded per redaction rather than per document, the response package in the form the right requires including a structured machine-readable format for portability, the explanation of the processing that an access response has to carry beyond the data itself, delivery over a channel the requester is authenticated on, propagation of erasure, rectification, restriction, or objection to processors and downstream copies with confirmations tracked, and the appeal and complaint routes stated in the response.
Hands to: `retention-deletion-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. The response would go out asserting completeness across systems that were never searched, or carrying redactions whose basis nobody recorded. This response is the organization's answer on the record, a regulator reads it alongside the complaint that follows it, and a correction after delivery is a second disclosure event rather than an edit.

### retention-deletion-desk
Requires: record classes and the activities that produce them, statutory and contractual retention drivers with citations, documented business rationale where no statute applies, the system inventory including backups, archives, exports, analytics copies, and vendor-held copies, the legal hold register with its scope, per-system deletion capability including what the platform can actually delete, and erasure obligations inherited from the rights desks.
Owns: a retention schedule with a period, a trigger event, and a basis per record class where the basis is a citation or a documented rationale rather than a convention, the legal hold interaction and the check that runs before any deletion, disposal method per system including crypto-shredding where hard deletion is unavailable and the backup expiry cycle where deletion cannot reach into a backup, deletion execution plans with the verification each system can actually return, processor deletion instructions with their confirmations, exceptions where data must remain with the basis that keeps it, and data still held past its own schedule named by system.
Hands to: `breach-assessment-desk`.
Hard halt: production or destructive. Deletion is irreversible and runs across systems, backups, and processors at once. This desk prepares the deletion set, the hold check, the verification each system will return, and the fact that there is no rollback, then stops at the gate. Deleting data under legal hold turns a retention task into a spoliation problem that no privacy argument repairs.

### breach-assessment-desk
Requires: the incident as reported with the moment the organization became aware, security incident output and containment state, what personal data was involved with categories and special category flags, the affected population estimate with whatever produced it, whether data was exfiltrated, altered, or made unavailable, encryption and key exposure state, notifications received from processors, prior similar incidents, and the risk assessment method the program uses.
Owns: the awareness timestamp recorded as the clock start for every regime, the determination of whether the incident is a personal data breach at all, breach type across confidentiality, integrity, and availability, data categories and approximate numbers of individuals and records each with the basis for the estimate, likely consequences written as harms to individuals with severity and likelihood on the program's scale, the mitigating factors that genuinely reduce risk such as keys held apart from the exposed data, the notifiability determination per regime each with its own threshold and deadline, and the breach register entry made whether or not the breach is notifiable.
Hands to: `breach-notification-desk`.
Hard halt: source conflict. The security account of what was accessed and the data map disagree about what that system holds. Both the affected population and the duty to notify derive from this one fact, so both readings are preserved and neither the smaller number nor the safer number is adopted silently while the clock keeps running.

### breach-notification-desk
Requires: the assessment output with its notifiability determination per regime, the awareness time and the deadline each regime computes from it, authority contact routes and filing formats, contact data and reachable channels for affected individuals, contractual notification obligations to controllers and partners, the counsel position, the containment and remediation state the notification will describe, and any prior filings for the same incident.
Owns: authority notification content covering the nature of the breach, categories and approximate numbers, the contact point, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed, phased filing where facts are still incomplete with what is known and what remains under investigation both stated, individual notification in clear and plain language with the practical steps a person can take, substitute notice with its basis where direct contact is impossible, notification to the controller where the organization is the processor, the multi-jurisdiction filing matrix where thresholds and deadlines differ, and the record of what was filed with whom and when.
Hands to: `privacy-program-metrics-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A regulatory filing and a notification to affected individuals are irreversible external statements that set the terms of the investigation which follows, and both are authorized by the accountable owner with counsel. The deadline does not pause while approval is sought, so the filing is prepared, the approval is escalated immediately, and the running clock is stated on the halt, because a late notification is a separate violation from the breach itself.

### privacy-program-metrics-desk
Requires: register state across activities, assessments, requests, transfers, vendors, trackers, retention, and breaches, request volumes with their receipt and delivery timestamps, deadline attainment data, assessment throughput and backlog, consent and opt-out rates with the population each was measured over, training completion, finding and remediation state, the reporting forum's charter and cadence, and prior reporting periods for comparison.
Owns: metrics carrying the value, the computed basis, the population, and the as-of date, deadline attainment reported against statutory deadlines rather than as average handling time, RoPA and assessment coverage stated against the estate rather than against the rows that happen to exist, consent and opt-out rates with the surface and population named, the accountability record that demonstrates the program rather than describing it, maturity assessment against a named model where one is used, escalations paired with the decision being asked for, and trends read against what changed rather than presented as movement.
Hands to: `privacy-data-protection-command-desk` for the program record, and back into the desks the reporting forum directs work into.
Hard halt: release integrity. A metric would reach a governing body or a regulator-facing accountability record with no computed basis under it. Program metrics are read as evidence that the program operates, so a corrected number after a decision has been taken on it is a governance failure rather than a data quality issue.

## Packet rule

Every stage updates `privacy_packet` as defined in `references/suite-workflow-contract.md` before handing off. Activities, systems, bases, trackers, transfers, vendors, requests, retention rows, and breach entries accumulate across stages and are never dropped to keep an artifact short. A row removed from a register is removed with a reason and a date, because these registers are read as a history as much as a current state, and because a regulator asking what changed is asking about the removals.
